name: Abū al-Ḥasan Saʿīd ibn Masʿada al-Mujāshiʿī
summary: Sībawayh's student, through whom al-Kitāb was handed on; author of Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, who went on to teach al-Kisāʾī's sons in Baghdad.
bio: Saʿīd ibn Masʿada came from Balkh, lived in Basra and was the 'middle' of the three Akhfashes. He was older than Sībawayh but learnt from him, and al-Kitāb reached the later grammarians only through him: Sībawayh read it with no one, and al-Jarmī and al-Māzinī read it with al-Akhfash.

Al-Zubaydī tells what followed the masʾala zunbūriyya in al-Akhfash's own words. Sībawayh sent for him on his way out of Iraq and told him what had happened; al-Akhfash went to Baghdad, prayed behind al-Kisāʾī, and put a hundred questions to him, faulting every answer. When al-Kisāʾī's students made to rise against him, al-Kisāʾī asked, 'By God, are you Abū al-Ḥasan Saʿīd ibn Masʿada?', embraced him, sat him at his side and asked him to teach his sons. At al-Kisāʾī's request al-Akhfash wrote his Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, on which al-Kisāʾī and then al-Farrāʾ modelled their own books.

He held views of his own against Sībawayh on many points, and later books quote 'al-Akhfash' as a voice between the two schools; in prosody he is credited with the sixteenth metre, the mutadārak. He died around 215/830.
uncertain: His death is given as 210, 211, 215 or 221 (825–836).
